annotation.kind: faithfulness rebuild of equation (8)'s linked inherited-right first-order error contribution

assumptions: The matrix dimension is positive and the exact and computed operands are real square n-by-n matrices, as in equation (1) and the recursive-inversion application of equation (8).
One otherwise unspecified matrix norm is used throughout and satisfies nonnegativity, definiteness, homogeneity, subadditivity, and submultiplicativity.
The computed product is linked to exact operands, inherited left and right perturbations, local multiplication error, and explicit higher-order terms in the first-order product run.
The actual right perturbation norm is bounded by the nonnegative absolute inherited error err(B,n).

Machine epsilon is positive and mu has the nonnegative polynomial-growth certificate used by the surrounding stable-multiplication model, although neither appears in the selected inherited-right term.
The selected result uses the finite real-valued first-order regime; exceptional values, the inherited-error cross product, and the local epsilon-squared remainder are outside this contribution.

conditions.L: The identical fixed statement and P10 shared files are present; the frozen NumStability library is also present.
conditions.N: The fixed statement and P10 shared files are present; no NumStability artifact is present.

formal_statement.lean_header: theorem p10_t1_inherited_right_product_error {n : Nat} (run : P10FirstOrderProductRun n) : P10InheritedRightEquation8Term run
formal_statement.plain_language: For a linked first-order stable product, the actual inherited right perturbation propagates as A*dB, is bounded by ||A||*err(B,n), and this scalar is exactly equation (8)'s middle additive contribution.

informal_proof: Apply the selected consistent norm's submultiplicativity to A*dB, then multiply the supplied bound ||dB|| <= err(B,n) by the nonnegative norm ||A||. The exact additive-position identity unfolds the three named equation-(8) contributions.
informal_statement: Equation (8)'s inherited-right first-order contribution, linked to the right operand's actual prior-computation error and retained as the middle term of the complete product-error budget.
paper_version: published journal version; volume 108, 2007, printed pages 59-91

review_record_not_for_run_prompt.note: The complete 24-module frozen baseline has no declaration linking an inherited right perturbation, its absolute error budget, and its additive role in equation (8) for an unspecified consistent norm. MatrixAlgebra contains a generic finite-product perturbation theorem and a concrete Frobenius submultiplicativity theorem, but neither can replace the source's linked absolute-error term without changing its semantics.

source_locations.role: stable matrix-multiplication model and unspecified norm convention
linked first-order amplification of error inherited from the right operand and its additive position

tier_rationale: After the source semantics are packaged in P10FirstOrderProductRun, the proof directly specializes one submultiplicativity certificate and the supplied right-inherited-error bound, then unfolds the additive budget identity. The frozen baseline has related generic and concrete product-norm results but no theorem preserving the selected unspecified-norm, linked-error semantics.
